units.title: Real Number System
units.intro: We meet **rational** and **irrational** numbers, change fractions to decimals and back, and find **square roots**.

pins.text: Real numbers: all rational and irrational numbers

cards.title: What is a rational number?
body: A **rational number** can be written as $\frac{a}{b}$.
Integers and fractions like $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{5}{6}$ are rational numbers.

cards.title: Write it as a over b
head: Number
As $\frac{a}{b}$

cards.why: Every integer can be written over 1. So $-9$ is rational.

cards.title: Fractions become decimals
body: To change a fraction into a decimal, **divide** the numerator by the denominator.

cards.title: Sharing sugar
cards.problem: Abdu divides 3 kg of sugar among 8 people. What is the share of each one?

cards.title: Sharing money
cards.problem: A woman shares 11 Nakfa among her 4 sons. What is each share?

cards.title: A division that never stops
cards.problem: Three women share 2 kg of sugar equally. How much does each get?

steps.text: The 6 repeats again and again. The division never stops.

cards.title: A bar for repeating digits
body: We write a **bar** over the digits that repeat.
Here the block 63 repeats and never ends.

cards.title: Two kinds of decimals
body: A **repeating decimal** never stops. Some digits repeat: $\frac{2}{3} = 0.666\ldots$, $\frac{7}{11} = 0.6363\ldots$

cards.title: Every rational number
body: A rational number is a terminating decimal or a repeating decimal.

cards.title: A quick test
body: Find the **prime factors** of the denominator.
- Any other prime factor (3, 7, 11 ...) → the decimal repeats.
Use the fraction in its simplest form.

cards.title: Is $\frac{7}{20}$ terminating?
cards.problem: Is $\frac{7}{20}$ a terminating or a repeating decimal?

cards.problem: Is $\frac{7}{12}$ a terminating or a repeating decimal?

cards.title: Your turn
cards.problem: Is $\frac{5}{12}$ terminating or repeating?

cards.title: 2 and 5 make 10
body: Our decimals count in tens, and $10 = 2 \times 5$.
So only the primes **2** and **5** let a decimal stop.

cards.title: Multiply by 10, 100, 1000
body: Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right.
The repeating part after the point stays the same.

cards.title: Haile's method: $0.\overline{6}$
cards.problem: Change $0.\overline{6}$ into a fraction.

steps.text: One digit repeats, so multiply by 10.
Subtract the first line from the second. The repeating parts cancel.

cards.title: Two digits repeat: $0.\overline{23}$
cards.problem: Change $0.\overline{23}$ into a fraction.

steps.text: Two digits repeat, so multiply by 100.

cards.problem: Change $1.2333\ldots$ into a fraction.

cards.title: Count the repeating digits
body: Then subtract, so the repeating tail disappears.

cards.problem: Change $0.1515\ldots$ into a fraction.

cards.title: Squares and their areas
body: A square with side 3 has $3 \times 3 = 9$ small squares.

cards.title: Square root
body: 6 is the square root of 36. 36 is 6 squared.

cards.title: Perfect squares
body: They are the squares of 3, 4 and 5.

cards.title: Square root by prime factors
cards.problem: Find $\sqrt{144}$.

steps.text: One group is the square root.

cards.title: Your turn
cards.problem: Find $\sqrt{225}$ by prime factors.

cards.title: Irrational numbers
body: Some decimals do **not** terminate and do **not** repeat.

cards.title: Irrational
body: An irrational number cannot be written as a ratio of two integers.
It is neither a repeating nor a terminating decimal.

cards.title: The real number family
body: Tap the dots to see each set.

cards.title: Real numbers
body: Rational numbers and irrational numbers together make the **real numbers**, $\mathbb{R}$.

lessons.title: Square root by the general method

cards.title: A square hall
cards.problem: A square hall has an area of 4489 m². How long is the hall?

steps.text: The side is $\sqrt{4489}$. Mark off the digits in groups of 2 from the right: 44 | 89.
The biggest square not more than 44 is $6 \times 6 = 36$. Write 6 on top.
Double 6 to get 12. Find a digit $x$ so that $12x \times x \le 889$.
Nothing is left. The root is 67.

cards.title: A bigger hall
cards.problem: Find $\sqrt{17424}$.

cards.title: Your turn: tiles
cards.problem: 5329 square tiles cover a square floor. How many tiles are in each row?

cards.title: General method steps
body: 1. Group the digits in pairs from the right.
2. Find the biggest square in the first group.
3. Subtract and bring down the next pair.
4. Double the root so far, then find the next digit.

Terminating test: factorize the denominator. Only 2s and 5s → it stops.
Repeating decimal → fraction: let it be $x$, multiply by 10, 100 or 1000, then subtract.
Always check a square root: multiply the answer by itself.

units.title: Equations and Inequalities
units.intro: We write **equations** from real life, solve **two equations together**, solve simple **quadratic equations**, and show **inequalities** on a number line.

cards.title: From a table to an equation
body: A grade 8 student is **2 years older** than a grade 6 student.
age in grade 8 = age in grade 6 + 2
Let $x$ = age in grade 6 and $y$ = age in grade 8.

cards.title: Words into maths
body: Haile has 3 Nakfa **less than twice** Seid's money.

cards.title: An equation is a balance
body: Both sides of $=$ have the same value.
Do the same thing to both sides, and it stays balanced.

cards.title: Solve for $a$
cards.problem: Solve $2a + 3 = 5$.

cards.title: Father and son
cards.problem: The father's age is 2 years more than three times his son's age. The sum of their ages is 98. How old is the father?

steps.text: Let the son's age be $x$. Then the father is $3x + 2$.

cards.answer: The father is 74 and the son is 24.

cards.title: Your turn
cards.problem: Semere is 3 years less than twice his sister's age. Five years ago the sum of their ages was 23. Find their ages now.

cards.title: Two facts, two letters
body: Fatuma and Semira have **15 Nakfa** together: $y + x = 15$.
Two equations with two letters are **simultaneous equations**.
We solve them together, by **elimination** or by **substitution**.

cards.title: Many pairs, one answer
body: Only one pair also makes $y - x = 3$ true.

cards.title: Ali's elimination
cards.problem: Solve $y + x = 15$ and $y - x = 3$.

steps.text: Add the two equations. $x + (-x) = 0$, so $x$ is eliminated.

cards.title: Multiply first
cards.problem: Solve $2y + 3x = 4$ and $5y - 2x = 29$.

steps.text: Adding does not remove a letter yet.
Multiply equation (1) by 2 and equation (2) by 3.

cards.title: Same size, opposite sign
body: Make one letter have the **same number** with **opposite signs**, like $+6x$ and $-6x$.

cards.title: Your turn
cards.problem: Solve $x + y = 14$ and $x - y = 4$.

cards.title: Almaz's substitution
cards.problem: Solve $y + x = 15$ and $y - x = 3$.

steps.text: Put $x + 3$ in place of $y$ in the first equation.

cards.title: Your turn
cards.problem: Solve $2x - y = 1$ and $y = 13 - 5x$.

cards.title: Which method?
body: **Elimination**: add or subtract the equations to remove one letter.
**Substitution**: write one letter from one equation and put it into the other.
Both methods give the same answer.

cards.title: Sugar and coffee
cards.problem: Yemane paid 260 Nakfa for 8 kg of sugar and 3 kg of coffee. Aster paid 400 Nakfa for 10 kg of sugar and 5 kg of coffee. Find the price of 1 kg of each.

steps.text: Let sugar = $x$ and coffee = $y$ Nakfa per kg.
Multiply the first by 5 and the second by 3.

cards.answer: Sugar 10 Nakfa per kg, coffee 60 Nakfa per kg

cards.title: Your turn: sheep and goats
cards.problem: Abraha bought 10 sheep and 15 goats for 3500 Nakfa. A sheep costs twice a goat. Find each price.

steps.text: The length is twice the width: $l = 2w$.

$a$, $b$, $c$ are numbers. The highest power of $x$ is 2.

Your turn
cards.problem: Solve $x(x - 2) = 0$.

body: So in $A \times B = 0$, one of them **must** be 0.

steps.text: Filled circle at $-1$, arrow to the right.

cards.title: Every point is a number
body: Between two rational numbers there are infinitely many other numbers.
Every point on the number line is a real number.

units.title: Graphs
units.intro: We plot **points**, draw **straight-line graphs**, find **intercepts**, solve two equations with a graph, and find the **slope** of a line.

cards.title: Two axes
body: The two axes meet at $(0, 0)$, the **origin**.
The axes cut the plane into **four quadrants**.

steps.text: 1st quadrant: right of the y-axis, above the x-axis.
2nd quadrant: left of the y-axis, above the x-axis.
3rd quadrant: left of the y-axis, below the x-axis.
4th quadrant: right of the y-axis, below the x-axis.

cards.title: Reading a point
body: The **first** number says how far **right** (+) or **left** (−).
The **second** number says how far **up** (+) or **down** (−).

cards.title: Where are these points?
body: $(3, 5)$ is in the 1st quadrant, $(-4, -2)$ in the 3rd, $(2, -6)$ in the 4th, $(-5, 6)$ in the 2nd.

cards.title: Go round like a clock backwards
body: Move to the left: **2nd**, down: **3rd**, right: **4th**.

cards.q: A point has a negative first number and a positive second number. Where is it?
cards.why: Left (−) and up (+) is the 2nd quadrant.

cards.title: Two points are enough

cards.title: Intercepts
body: The **x-intercept** is where the line crosses the x-axis: $(a, 0)$.
The **y-intercept** is where the line crosses the y-axis: $(0, b)$.

The point where they **cross** is the solution.

cards.title: Lines that never meet

units.title: Transformations
units.intro: We learn two **transformations**: **reflection** (a flip in a mirror line) and **translation** (a slide).

cards.title: Transformation
body: A **transformation** is a change in position, size or shape.

cards.title: A mirror
body: Look in a plane mirror. You see your **image**.
Raise your right hand: the image raises the hand on the same side, but it looks like a left hand.
Step back: the image also steps back.

steps.text: Triangle PQR and the mirror line (here the y-axis).
Each point goes to the other side, the same distance from the line. $P_1$ is the image of $P$.

cards.title: Line of reflection
body: The mirror line is the **line of reflection**.
A point and its image are the **same distance** from the line.
If you fold along the line, a point lands on its image.

cards.title: Find the mirror line
cards.problem: The image of $A(-2, 4)$ under a reflection is $A_1(2, 4)$. Where is the line of reflection?

steps.text: The two points have the same $y$: 4.
So the line of reflection is $x = 0$, the y-axis.

cards.q: A point A is ON the line of reflection. Where is its image?
cards.why: A point on the mirror line does not move.

cards.title: Fold and match
body: Imagine folding the paper along the mirror line.
Each point lands exactly on its image.

cards.title: Sliding
body: A **translation** moves a shape in a straight line in one direction.
All points move the **same distance** in the **same direction**.
An **arrow** shows the direction and the distance.

steps.text: The translation takes $(0, 0)$ 2 units up and 1 unit left, to $(-1, 2)$.
Do the same to $A(0, 2)$: left 1, up 2. The image is $(-1, 4)$.

cards.title: Coordinates
body: Right → add to $x$. Left → take from $x$.
Up → add to $y$. Down → take from $y$.

units.title: Statistics and Probability
units.intro: We find the **mean**, **median** and **mode**, measure how **spread out** data are, and learn **probability**.

cards.title: Average
body: The **mean** (arithmetic mean) is the **average** of the data.
We use it every day: average cost, average speed, average rainfall.

cards.title: Three measures
body: **Median** = the middle value when the values are in order.
**Mode** = the value that comes most often.

steps.text: There are 10 numbers, so there are two middle numbers: 6 and 7.
The bars show how many students got each mark.
85 has the highest bar (6 students). The mode is 85.

body: Saron and Bahlbi both have mean 80.
